title: C5 — identity
description: platform -> inference, interface. Provisioning a person crosses two layers; this is why. Each operation below is exposed as its own endpoint by the layer named in its title — nobody calls a neighbour's database instead. See docs/ADR.md ADR-010 for why this contract exists at all.

principal_id.description: Opaque identifier for the person or service this credential is for. The inference layer does not resolve this to an identity — that is the interface layer's job, on its own side of this same contract.

budget.description: Spend ceiling, in the currency the deployment bills in.

allowed_key_policies.description: Which of the two credential families this principal may ever be issued. A principal who should never reach a third-party provider gets ['local-only'] here — not a runtime check downstream.

password.description: Optional. If omitted on first creation, the interface generates one and returns it in create_account_response -- there is no other operation in this contract that issues a login credential, so this is the only time it is ever knowable. Omitted on a call that updates an account which already exists, the password is left untouched.

role.description: Optional, defaults to 'user'. Applied only when the account is being created for the first time -- a call that updates an existing account never changes its role.

password.description: Present only when a credential was just set: generated on first creation if the caller did not supply one, or echoed back when the caller did. Absent when this call updated an existing account without touching its password.

has_credential.description: Whether a virtual key has been linked via link_credential. Never the key itself, or any part of it -- this operation is a status check, not a second way to read a secret link_credential already wrote.

link_credential_request.title: interface: link an issued credential to an account

virtual_key.description: The actual secret the inference layer issued (this contract's issue_credential_response does not carry it back — LiteLLM's /key/generate does, directly, to whoever requested it). The interface stores it to call the gateway on the account's behalf; this operation is what replaces writing that secret into the interface's database by any means other than its own API.

ensure_model_catalog_entry_request.title: interface: register a model in the visibility catalog
ensure_model_catalog_entry_request.description: Global and idempotent: one call per model that exists in the deployment, not one per account. A caller that repeats this call for every account it provisions is not wrong -- the operation is safe to repeat -- but it is calling it far more often than the data changes.

configure_upstream_request.title: interface: point the interface at the inference gateway
configure_upstream_request.description: Global, one-time, deploy-time bootstrap -- not part of provisioning any single account. A deployment that never calls this has no model dropdown, and every account it provisions is otherwise complete.
